- Substituents on the pyrimidine ring:

  - Position 4: OC (methoxy group)
  - Position 5: -c2cnc(OC)c(OC)c2 (a substituted pyrimidine ring attached at position 5? Wait, let's check numbering. Pyrimidine is 1,3-diazine. Usually numbered N1, C2, N3, C4, C5, C6. Here it's `c1c(OC)cc(...)nc1`. So N at pos 1, C(OC) at pos 2, C at pos 3, C at pos 4, C(subst) at pos 5, N at pos 6. Wait, SMILES parsing: c1 c(OC) c c (-c2...) n c1. So positions: 1=N, 2=C(OC), 3=C, 4=C, 5=C(subst), 6=N. Actually, standard pyrimidine numbering might differ, but it's a di-substituted pyrimidine with two methoxy groups and one bromomethyl group, plus a fused/linked pyrimidine.)
  - Position 6: CCOC(=O) (ethoxycarbonyl group)
